data.title: Have Insiders Sold Serve Robotics Shares Recently?
data.description:
We'd be surprised if Serve Robotics Inc. (NASDAQ:SERV) shareholders haven't noticed that the Co-Founder, Ali Kashani, recently sold US$147k worth of stock at US$2.38 per share. On the bright side, that sale was only 2.3% of their holding, so we doubt it's very meaningful, on its own.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Serve Robotics Insider Transactions Over The Last Year

In fact, the recent sale by Co-Founder Ali Kashani was not their only sale of Serve Robotics shares this year. Earlier in the year, they fetched US$9.29 per share in a -US$245k sale. While insider selling is a negative, to us, it is more negative if the shares are sold at a lower price. It's of some comfort that this sale was conducted at a price well above the current share price, which is US$2.40. So it may not shed much light on insider confidence at current levels.

Insiders in Serve Robotics didn't buy any shares in the last year. You can see the insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last year depicted in the chart below. If you click on the chart, you can see all the individual transactions, including the share price, individual, and the date!

View our latest analysis for Serve Robotics

I will like Serve Robotics better if I see some big insider buys. While we wait, check out this free list of undervalued and small cap stocks with considerable, recent, insider buying.

Insider Ownership Of Serve Robotics

For a common shareholder, it is worth checking how many shares are held by company insiders. I reckon it's a good sign if insiders own a significant number of shares in the company. Insiders own 4.5% of Serve Robotics shares, worth about US$9.7m, according to our data. Whilst better than nothing, we're not overly impressed by these holdings.

So What Does This Data Suggest About Serve Robotics Insiders?

Insiders haven't bought Serve Robotics stock in the last three months, but there was some selling. And even if we look at the last year, we didn't see any purchases. When you consider that most companies have higher levels of insider ownership, we're a little wary. So we're not rushing to buy, to say the least. So while it's helpful to know what insiders are doing in terms of buying or selling, it's also helpful to know the risks that a particular company is facing. data.title: Only Four Days Left To Cash In On Prudential Financial's (NYSE:PRU) Dividend
data.description:
It looks like Prudential Financial, Inc. (NYSE:PRU) is about to go ex-dividend in the next 4 days. The ex-dividend date is usually set to be one business day before the record date, which is the cut-off date on which you must be present on the company's books as a shareholder in order to receive the dividend. The ex-dividend date is important as the process of settlement involves a full business day. So if you miss that date, you would not show up on the company's books on the record date. This means that investors who purchase Prudential Financial's shares on or after the 24th of November will not receive the dividend, which will be paid on the 10th of December.

The company's next dividend payment will be US$1.40 per share, on the back of last year when the company paid a total of US$5.60 to shareholders. Based on the last year's worth of payments, Prudential Financial stock has a trailing yield of around 4.6% on the current share price of US$121.54. Dividends are a major contributor to investment returns for long term holders, but only if the dividend continues to be paid. That's why we should always check whether the dividend payments appear sustainable, and if the company is growing.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Dividends are usually paid out of company profits, so if a company pays out more than it earned then its dividend is usually at greater risk of being cut. Prudential Financial paid out 50% of its earnings to investors last year, a normal payout level for most businesses.

When a company paid out less in dividends than it earned in profit, this generally suggests its dividend is affordable. The lower the % of its profit that it pays out, the greater the margin of safety for the dividend if the business enters a downturn.

View our latest analysis for Prudential Financial

Click here to see the company's payout ratio, plus analyst estimates of its future dividends.

Have Earnings And Dividends Been Growing?

Stocks with flat earnings can still be attractive dividend payers, but it is important to be more conservative with your approach and demand a greater margin for safety when it comes to dividend sustainability. If business enters a downturn and the dividend is cut, the company could see its value fall precipitously. With that in mind, we're not enthused to see that Prudential Financial's earnings per share have remained effectively flat over the past five years. We'd take that over an earnings decline any day, but in the long run, the best dividend stocks all grow their earnings per share.

Another key way to measure a company's dividend prospects is by measuring its historical rate of dividend growth. Prudential Financial has delivered an average of 7.2% per year annual increase in its dividend, based on the past 10 years of dividend payments.

The Bottom Line

Should investors buy Prudential Financial for the upcoming dividend? Prudential Financial's earnings are effectively flat over recent years, even as the company pays out more than half of its earnings to shareholders as dividends. We think there are likely better opportunities out there.

However if you're still interested in Prudential Financial as a potential investment, you should definitely consider some of the risks involved with Prudential Financial. Our analysis shows 1 warning sign for Prudential Financial and you should be aware of this before buying any shares.

data.title: Revenue Beat: H World Group Limited Exceeded Revenue Forecasts By 5.8% And Analysts Are Updating Their Estimates
data.description:
A week ago, H World Group Limited (NASDAQ:HTHT) came out with a strong set of quarterly numbers that could potentially lead to a re-rate of the stock. Results were good overall, with revenues beating analyst predictions by 5.8% to hit CN¥7.8b. Statutory earnings per share (EPS) came in at CN¥5.63, some 4.1% above whatthe analysts had expected. This is an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance in its report, look at what experts are forecasting for next year, and see if there has been any change to expectations for the business. We thought readers would find it interesting to see the analysts latest (statutory) post-earnings forecasts for next year.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

After the latest results, the 20 analysts covering H World Group are now predicting revenues of CN¥29.3b in 2027. If met, this would reflect a credible 6.9% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to step up 19% to CN¥20.85. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of CN¥28.9b and earnings per share (EPS) of CN¥20.39 in 2027. So the consensus seems to have become somewhat more optimistic on H World Group's earnings potential following these results.

View our latest analysis for H World Group

There's been no major changes to the consensus price target of US$62.89, suggesting that the improved earnings per share outlook is not enough to have a long-term positive impact on the stock's valuation. There's another way to think about price targets though, and that's to look at the range of price targets put forward by analysts, because a wide range of estimates could suggest a diverse view on possible outcomes for the business. Currently, the most bullish analyst values H World Group at US$68.00 per share, while the most bearish prices it at US$55.98. Even so, with a relatively close grouping of estimates, it looks like the analysts are quite confident in their valuations, suggesting H World Group is an easy business to forecast or the the analysts are all using similar assumptions.

One way to get more context on these forecasts is to look at how they compare to both past performance, and how other companies in the same industry are performing. We would highlight that H World Group's revenue growth is expected to slow, with the forecast 5.5% annualised growth rate until the end of 2027 being well below the historical 16% p.a. growth over the last five years. By way of comparison, the other companies in this industry with analyst coverage are forecast to grow their revenue at 9.3% per year. So it's pretty clear that, while revenue growth is expected to slow down, the wider industry is also expected to grow faster than H World Group.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing here is that the analysts upgraded their earnings per share estimates, suggesting that there has been a clear increase in optimism towards H World Group following these results. Fortunately, the analysts also reconfirmed their revenue estimates, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Although our data does suggest that H World Group's revenue is expected to perform worse than the wider industry. The consensus price target held steady at US$62.89, with the latest estimates not enough to have an impact on their price targets.

Stryker Investment Narrative Recap

To own Stryker, you typically need to believe in a defensive medtech story built on procedure demand, robotics adoption and steady margin work rather than big swings. According to duarte_EM, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the appeal sits in Mako expansion, recurring consumables and bolt on deals supported by an ageing population. The recent quarter showed 10.3% adjusted EPS growth from margin gains and cost control, which keeps that thesis intact.

In the short term, the key swing factor looks like execution in robotics and MedSurg while working through softer hip and knee procedures plus supply bottlenecks. Cyber and SAP related disruption, together with high debt and recent insider selling, remain operational and sentiment risks. The latest robotics updates and profit momentum do not remove those issues, but they show the current playbook still working.

The appointment of James E. Davis to Stryker’s board from January 2027 is the most relevant fresh announcement here. He brings CEO experience from Quest Diagnostics, previous leadership at InSightec, and two decades across General Electric’s healthcare and aviation arms, including running the MRI business. That background sits close to Stryker’s mix of capital equipment, software and hospital customers.

This board addition intersects directly with the firm’s catalysts around robotics, smart beds and MedSurg technology. duarte_EM argues the story leans on disciplined M&A, recurring consumables and a defensive growth profile, and Davis’ track record across diagnostics and medical devices may help oversight of those execution priorities. For investors watching governance, his arrival adds another experienced voice to an already seasoned and largely independent board.

Using revenue growth of 8.0% a year and a future profit margin of 14.4%, the narrative from duarte_EM arrives at a fair value of $311.21 for Stryker by assuming the business can compound earnings at that pace while maintaining what is viewed as a quality medtech profile.

Exploring Other Perspectives

Some analysts see Stryker very differently. Where the baseline leans on steady robotics and MedSurg execution, the most pessimistic voices focus on peripheral vascular supply problems and legal overhangs. Those forecasts had revenue at about US$31.8b and earnings near US$6.5b by 2029, yet still supported one of the lowest price targets. data.title: Is SELLAS Life Sciences Group (SLS) Fully Valued As REGAL Trial Success Lifts Expectations?
data.description:
SELLAS Life Sciences Group (SLS) is back in focus after its Phase 3 REGAL trial for cancer vaccine galinpepimut S in acute myeloid leukemia hit the primary overall survival endpoint, sparking heavy trading interest.

The share price reaction has been sharp and fast. SELLAS Life Sciences Group has a 7 day share price return of 113.18% and a year to date share price gain of 312.64%. The 1 year total shareholder return is very large compared with the recent 1 day pullback of 6.27%. This signals powerful momentum that has cooled slightly following the $150.0m follow on equity offering priced at a discount.

Capture this kind of sharp biotech catalyst early by scanning our 37 healthcare AI stocks, which are already moving on clinical data, regulatory milestones, or fresh trial readouts.

For SELLAS Life Sciences Group, the REGAL win and the discounted equity raise pull in opposite directions. Is the latest surge pricing in a stronger underlying business, or a rapid reset in sentiment that still needs testing through valuation?

Preferred Price-to-Book of 27.8x: Is it justified?

SELLAS Life Sciences Group closed at $17.95, yet the market is valuing the equity at a P/B ratio of 27.8x, far above typical biotech levels. That kind of premium signals that traders are pricing in a very optimistic future relative to the company’s current balance sheet.

P/B compares the market value of the shares with the accounting book value of net assets. It is often used for early stage or pre revenue biotechs where earnings are still negative. For SELLAS Life Sciences Group, a 27.8x multiple indicates investors are paying a high price today for assets that currently generate no reported revenue and a loss of $35.76m.

The gap to peers is wide. The US Biotechs group trades on an average P/B of 1.6x, while SELLAS Life Sciences Group sits at 27.8x. This is a very large premium that suggests the market is assigning a far richer valuation than the sector norm and leaves little room for disappointment if clinical or funding milestones do not line up with expectations.

data.title: Star Bulk Carriers (SBLK) Reports Its Highest Quarterly Dividend Since 2022
data.description:
• Star Bulk Carriers (NasdaqGS:SBLK) reported its highest quarterly dividend since 2022, returning cash to shareholders from recent results.
  • The group completed a multi year newbuilding fleet program, marking the end of a significant capex cycle on new vessels.
  • Management announced a dual listing on Euronext Athens alongside a sizeable equity raise and a new strategic partnership.
  • This mix of record dividend, completed fleet program, fresh equity and new partnership now needs weighing against the rest of our work. Our analysis turns up 1 warning sign for Star Bulk Carriers as well.

Star Bulk Carriers runs a large fleet that ships dry bulk commodities like iron ore and coal across global trade routes, so a completed vessel program and fresh capital matter directly for how it can compete for long haul contracts in this space. As one of the larger US listed players with a market cap of about US$3.2b, its operating scale is central to how investors may read these updates.

Is Star Bulk Carriers's dividend sustainable? Check out what every dividend investor needs to know in our dividend analysis.

Star Bulk Carriers dividend news puts its cash-return story to the test

The investment story for Star Bulk Carriers is that a low cost fleet and cash flow linked payout policy can turn freight cycles into consistent shareholder distributions, and this latest US$1.00 dividend puts that idea under the spotlight.

The policy to distribute 100% of free or operating cash flow subject to a minimum cash balance, combined with over US$3.1b of capital allocation actions since 2021...

See how the full story points towards a $34.44 fair value for Star Bulk Carriers.

The higher dividend and 23 quarter streak support the view that Star Bulk Carriers' cash generation model is operating as intended, with management choosing to send a large share of earnings out rather than holding higher liquidity. Finishing the newbuilding program and partnering with Hermes World Maritime also aligns with the Narrative focus on fleet efficiency as a way to protect margins against volatile freight rates that peers like Golden Ocean or Genco Shipping also face.

The equity raise and dual listing can suggest a different perspective for more cautious investors, since issuing new shares while paying a high dividend highlights how sensitive this payout formula can be to future spot conditions. Analysts have already identified dividend sustainability as a risk, so any weaker dry bulk demand or higher fuel costs could lead this cash flow linked policy to reset quickly.

Ultimately, interpreting a record dividend funded by a fully renewed fleet and fresh equity depends on each investor’s view of where Star Bulk Carriers is heading, which is exactly what its Narrative is designed to present.
